messages:
Aisha Patel: Heads up — VioletWorks trial hit a 38% drop in active pipelines this week, flagged for potential downgrade at renewal. Saw support ticket about slow response on batch inference. cc @Ben_CSM :warning:
Tom Nguyen: thanks — renewal in 21 days? any usage thresholds crossed?
Aisha Patel: renewal date 2026-04-12, usage peaked week 1 then steady decline. They hit inference error spikes during long sequences. Customer said "costs feel unpredictable".
Ben_CSM: ok. propose MicroSave plan:
- 2-week grace credits (20% usage) to buy time
- Quick enablement call + tailored prompts
- Low-effort config change: pin quantized model variant for cost predictability
- Re-route heavy jobs to scheduled batch window
Tom Nguyen: love it. can we add a downgrade swap path if they still want to leave? Minimal friction: export data, preserve keys, and offer one-month roll-back.
Ella (product): we can enable temporary feature-flag to reduce concurrency and throttle long requests. I'll open a canary flag. Also can ship a short onboarding checklist to reduce errors.
onboarding-bot: Playbook link: https://playbooks.internal/redwood/microsave-v1 — steps, email templates, call script
Ben_CSM: call script snippet:
```
Agenda: 15m
1) Recap pain points
2) Offer 20% credit + model pin
3) Walk through seq length limits + batching
4) Agree on 2-week success metric (>=70% baseline usage)
```
Aisha Patel: i'll schedule call for Tue 10am PT. Ben, can you own follow-up? :handshake:
Ben_CSM: got it. I'll prepare a targeted prompt-set + quick eval to show quality parity with quantized model.
Tom Nguyen: ops question — who runs the downgrade swap? CS or infra?
Ben_CSM: CS initiates, infra runs the swap. I'll add Jira ticket and set runbook link.
Aisha Patel: final ask — prepare a short customer-facing note explaining cost predictability + rollback. Use plain language. no legalese.
Ella (product): will draft, keep it <150 words. share for sign-off.
onboarding-bot: created ticket #CS-7629
Ben_CSM: :thumbsup: moving to action. goal: prevent churn, aim for re-activation not retention-only.
